pr_title: Enable Portable ThreadPool events to be written using NativeRuntimeEventSource
pr_body:
This removes the temporary solution that the portable ThreadPool was using to emit events from managed side. Specifically, the following changes were made: 
* Change the GUID of NativeRuntimeEventSource to match the native provider (Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntime)
* Remove the hacks in EventPipe and EventSource that existed for the temporary solution
* Add endpoints in XplatEventSourceLogger that correspond to each managed event that acts as a sink for forwarding events to LTTng
*  Change the genRuntimeEventSources.py script to not generate events for the hand-written ThreadPool events. 

Fix #45384

cc @brianrob @josalem @kouvel @noahfalk @tommcdon

issue_context.title: Support Managed Threadpool Diagnostics
issue_context.body:
The goal is to maintain parity with existing diagnostics for the native thread pool.  Currently the concrete work for this item is:

- [ ] Make NativeRuntimeEventSource.cs as a general way of sending runtime events from managed side, as opposed to what it is now
- [x] Make sure the events being fired from the managed ThreadPool is being fired correctly.
- [ ] Fix EventListener deadlock that can occur as part of enabling managed threadpool events through EventListener 
- [ ] Make sure EventListeners can subscribe to managed threadpool events
- [ ] Test LTTng events can still get fired from managed threadpool under the Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntime provider

review_comments: Lets restore and update this comment. I assume the rationale is that we want EventListeners to be able to subscribe to events emitted by native code which may come before the first event emitted via managed code.

If we are going to be hand-writing interop code I would add a hardy comment here that describes why this EventSource is different from other EventSources and what devs need to do implementation-wise if they want to start using new events.

If I recall correctly, this is here because otherwise events that are written by the runtime end up getting pushed to this `EventListener` and then back down to LTTng.  This only happens when COMPlus_EnableEventLog=1, and then you only see it if you're capturing via LTTng I believe.  The details are a bit fuzzy...

This was preventing the provider to get enabled when only LTTng is specified via COMPlus_EnableEventLog=1. I moved this check to `OnEvenWritten` check instead so that they don't get forwarded as EventSourceEvent.
Does something not work if we leave this in place?
This is now merged with NativeRuntimeEventSource, which already has this parameterized constructor.

I would clarify in the comment why WriteEvent() APIs are not being used here, that it causes double logging because of special case handling of this source in the EventListener code and gives us strongly typed LTTng events rather than the default LTTng handling that other EventSources get.
Is `NativeRuntimeEventSource` now guaranteed to always be initialized, even just for a console app?
I may have missed it, but what ensures that `IsEnabled` returns true?

Sorry, I don't think I quite got what you're asking here.. Do you mean what ensures that the DoCommand callback is received for the NativeRuntimeEventSource?

NativeRuntimeEventSource registers itself with the native runtime upon initialization, and it will receive callback from the runtime from the standard callback handler, just like how any other managed EventSources receive callbacks when being enabled.

Essentially the runtime "thinks" there are two providers -- the native provider whose callback is the EtwCallbackCommon function and the managed provider whose callback is the managed callback function in EventSource.

Lets add text here that says why we aren't forwarding these events. The comment can point to the native Lttng handling code and mention how we generate different output for these special cased events vs. what would be generated for any other EventSource.
Also we should add that they need to update the getRuntimeEventSources.py to make sure that script doesn't autogenerate a duplicate method that throws NotImplementedException.
